doc.title: Harry Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Playing for an older audience; future of the jazz audience
summary: Shades tune choice not style; jazz parties will fade but clubs and festivals draw younger crowds.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: No. I don’t change my playing any. I might shade the tune selection a little bit to what I think the audience might like. I mean I know, not that I am any expert on bebop heads, but I know enough that if I’m in front of an audience that I think would like that I can play some bebop heads for them. Play “Groovin’ High” for that audience and for this audience play “Whispering,” and take the same style solo that I would take in either one.
That would be a good trick. Does it worry you at all?
You know the question. It’s almost like you guys have talked about this, probably recently, that the audience out there may not be around forever.

Well it doesn’t necessarily worry me that much because there are a lot of places that I play that have a lot younger audiences. The jazz parties — I don’t think that they’re going to carry on too many more years because the audience is getting fairly up there in years, and also it’s so expensive to come to them that the younger audiences are not going to be able to afford it. But there are a lot of clubs and a lot of the single day festivals or week-long festivals that you buy one ticket at a time for, that the younger audiences do go to and so I’m not terribly concerned.
